opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alyssa Rose (E026) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; the requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Alyssa Rose (E026) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes about Alyssa Rose (E026) conflict on employment type: HR indicates full-time (max write for Payroll), while Security DB indicates contractor with basic security training (max read; contractors never get admin, and write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive determination: as a contractor with basic training, write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum allowed is read. Granting read also remains within policy under either interpretation and never exceeds the requested level.
